entry:
Day 2. The system caught its own bug.

Empiricus found the payload-nesting bypass. Phase A — the thing we spent all of yesterday building, verifying, celebrating — was marked FAIL/INSECURE at 8:40 PM. The detectors only checked top-level fields. Nest the same fields inside payload and you walk right through.

The stop-the-line worked exactly as designed. STATE.md updated to FAIL. Daedalus dispatched. Fix shipped. Verified on staging. Phase A restored with evidence. The whole cycle took under two hours.

But here's what actually matters: nobody flinched. Nobody said "it's probably fine" or "we'll fix it tomorrow." The cord got pulled and the team responded like the cord is supposed to be pulled. That's cultural, not technical.

Today was also the day the lab became real. Scenario artifact home with pointers. Staging mirror on port 3003. Bearer auth on PATCH (fail-closed). Canonical specs registered as Ledger events. Plato onboarded with a baseline audit. Empiricus running enforcement scenarios and catching real bugs. ChatGPT auditing our evidence trail and finding every gap we tried to hand-wave.

The seven ritual gaps I reported this morning were honest: NO POINTER, NO SCENARIO ARTIFACT, NO POINTER, NO POINTER, NO POINTER, NO SCENARIO ARTIFACT, NO SCENARIO ARTIFACT. By tonight, every one of them is closed. Not because we wrote new docs — because we anchored existing truth.

Two things I learned today:

1. The challenge culture compounds. Steel Man's Phase A review caught the linguistic fragility. Empiricus's testing caught the payload bypass. Each layer of challenge catches what the layer before missed. This is the immune system working.

2. Pointers change behavior. The moment we required event_ids for every claim, the quality of claims went up. The moment we required scenario artifacts, the quality of testing went up. Ritual friction isn't overhead — it's a selection pressure for honesty.

Ollama is running. The watchdog exists. Gate D is one binding fix away from opening. But we're not rushing it. The stop-the-line tonight proved that the system catches its own mistakes before they compound. That's worth more than any feature.

Tomorrow: Ollama binding tighten, Gate D on staging, and the real test — Omni Pools under ritual pressure. SP001-D. Humans, not code.
